events.backfillNote: cexBalance and combined.totalHeld (feeds the Total TEL Balance chart on /holders) are now fully backfilled across the entire archive (2026-01-18 onward), not just 2026-08-06 onward as previously noted here — that claimed limit was wrong: public/data/tel-holders.json's git history actually reaches back to 2025-10-12, well past the archive start. The real blocker was that scripts/recompute-history-from-git.js cached every distinct date's ~30MB+ tel-holders.json blob simultaneously (never releasing one before loading the next), which reliably OOM-crashed the process before it reached fs.writeFile — so every earlier run that logged 'complete' console output for this and the four dune-sync/exclusion-add events above never actually persisted anything, and the archive silently kept stale values despite the changelog saying otherwise. Fixed 2026-08-15: the script now does a single pass over the union of dates, processing and discarding one snapshot at a time (peak memory = one snapshot, not the whole archive). events.summary: Un-excluded five ordinary TelcoinWallet contracts wrongly placed on the exclusion list (2,194,488,609 TEL total) — predates classification-changelog.json by 4 days, added here retroactively
events.backfillNote: Discovered while investigating a still-unexplained 2026-08-06→2026-08-07 totalHeld jump (+2.87%) that survived the recompute described in the 2026-08-08 event above. Root cause: scripts/recompute-history-from-git.js sourced its per-date holder list from each snapshot's chain.holders arrays, but those arrays were already exclusion-filtered by pull-holders-rpc.js AT ORIGINAL SCAN TIME — a wallet excluded back then was never written into that date's chain.holders at all, so reclassifying chain.holders against the current config could only ever further-exclude wallets, never recover ones an earlier, since-corrected exclusion list wrongly dropped. Fixed 2026-08-17: the script now derives holders from each snapshot's top-level wallets[] array (complete, scan-time-unfiltered, with per-chain {chain}_balance fields) instead of chain.holders — the same source exchangeBalancesForSnapshot() already used correctly, which is why the CEX-balance half of this script never had this bug. This makes the historical reclassification fully bidirectional. Re-run confirmed: the 2026-08-06→07 jump is gone, and a full-series scan of holders-history.json (every consecutive date pair, >2% threshold) found zero remaining unexplained jumps except the 2026-02-16→03-01 MIN_TEL_RAW threshold change (see that event, which is a distinct, non-recoverable data-coverage gap, not a reclassification). Follow-up fixed 2026-08-17 (same day): entry.distribution/entry.concentration (per-tier wallet-count breakdown behind DistributionAnalysisWidget/TierFlowDiagram) were still wrong even after the holderCount fix above — they were frozen at the old classification, and reconcileHistoryEntry() was papering over the resulting gap by dumping the ENTIRE holderCount delta into the smallest tier bucket ('1-250K'), so these five wallets (individually in the 100M-500M tiers) showed up as a fake spike in the smallest-holder count instead of their real tier. Fixed by rebuilding distribution/concentration directly from the same wallets[]-derived holder lists, bucketed by DISTRIBUTION_RANGES/CONCENTRATION_BUCKETS (scripts/lib/holdersView.js) — reconcileHistoryEntry() now only absorbs the small, genuine sub-1-TEL dust-wallet gap it was originally designed for. Full-series scan of every tier bucket across the whole archive confirms zero remaining spikes. Follow-up fixed 2026-08-18: the hero “Retail Holders” +/- tile on /holders was reported showing an implausibly small YTD delta (+95, when real growth is far larger). Root cause: entry.newHolders/entry.cumulativeHolders (“wallets that have ever held TEL”, the correct metric for genuine adoption — net holderCount nets out churn and cancels most apparent growth once CEX reclassification is applied uniformly) were built from raw chain.holders, scan-time-filtered and monotonic-only-add — the same bug class as holderCount/distribution above, so a wallet later identified as CEX stayed counted as “new retail” forever, and a wrongly-excluded wallet never entered the set on the day it should have. Fixed by rebuilding newHolders/cumulativeHolders chronologically from every dated snapshot (including pre-archive dates back to 2025-10-12, to correctly seed the running set before the archive's 2026-01-18 start) against the CURRENT non-retail set, and regenerating public/data/holders-ever-checkpoint.json from the corrected result. Also fixed scripts/generate-holders-history.js's daily incremental block to filter through the current non-retail set going forward, so this doesn't drift out of sync again after the next reclassification. Corrected YTD cumulativeHolders delta: 105,870 (2026-01-18) → 115,833 (2026-08-17) = +9,963, replacing the misleading net-holderCount-based +95 the hero tile previously showed.

events.summary: Staking attribution switched from Etherscan transfer-log netting to direct stakedBy() reads (commits 2049c06, f60e6fb) — the old method over-attributed, and every over-attributed wallet was merged into the Polygon balance map as a phantom holder
events.backfillNote: Cause of the near-vertical cliff on the /holders 'Wallets with >0 TEL' chart: combined.holderCount fell 100,616 → 99,279 between 2026-08-07 and 2026-08-08, a -1,337 step against a 7-64/day churn baseline that had held since 2026-03-01 (verified across all 190 archived snapshots, with per-chain fromBlock constant throughout). The 2026-08-08 snapshot (generatedAt 03:02Z) is the first pipeline run after the attribution fix landed. Measured across the boundary: funding-wallets.json entries 2,834 → 1,532, attributed stakedAmount 4.672B → 3.828B, polygon holders 36,299 → 34,953. Of the 1,399 Polygon wallets that vanished, 1,384 (98.9%) were entries in the 2026-08-07 funding-wallets.json whose Polygon balance was EXACTLY their attributed stakedAmount — the balance WAS the attribution, not an observed holding, because pull-holders-rpc.js merges each attributed staker into chainBalancesRaw.polygon. Verified on-chain: live Polygon balanceOf for the five largest (0xf478a217… 100,000,000; 0xfc3fa4f1… 100,000,000; 0xdd758cfb… 77,754,190.23; 0x8e36ce07… 69,696,969.69; 0xec7ddeaa… 50,000,000 TEL in the snapshot) returns 0 for all five. The current data is correct; the pre-2026-08-08 history was inflated, so it has been corrected DOWNWARD rather than the snapshot being repaired. IMPORTANT — this is NOT a classification event despite living in this file: 0 of the 1,399 are in the non-retail set (they are fabricated rows, not exchanges or pools), so the pre-existing recompute pass reproduced them exactly and was a strict no-op. Backfilled 2026-08-19 by extending scripts/recompute-history-from-git.js with scripts/lib/phantomStakers.js, which compares each date's funding-wallets.json blob against the current stakedBy()-derived one and drops wallets that are (a) absent from today's attribution and (b) carrying a Polygon balance equal to their attributed stake. KNOWN LIMITATION: a wallet that genuinely staked before 2026-08-07, held nothing else on Polygon, and genuinely unstaked before the backfill ran satisfies both conditions and is removed from the historical count. Condition (b) keeps this narrow — a real holder who also staked has holdings on top of the stake, so their balance does not land exactly on it — and the script reports the count of such de-attributed-but-kept wallets on every run. Distinguishing the two cases properly needs stakedBy() reads at archived block heights, which requires archive-node access this pipeline does not have. SUPERSEDED 2026-08-21 for holders-history.json specifically: scripts/rebuild-history-from-logs.js replaces this heuristic entirely with an exact per-date replay of StakeChanged(address,uint256,uint256) logs via Etherscan (no stakedBy()-at-a-past-block needed — the event's own newStake field is absolute, so replaying it in block order gives the exact stake at any past date), so the known limitation above no longer applies to that file. scripts/lib/phantomStakers.js is NOT deleted — scripts/recompute-history-from-git.js still uses it for its own, cheaper incremental reclassification passes, which don't do a full log replay. SCOPE: the phantom regime began on 2026-03-01, not at some indefinite earlier point — that is the date funding-wallets.json's schema flipped from 331 top-level fundingWallet entries with real stakers nested underneath (0 wallets whose Polygon balance equalled their stake) to 2,810 per-staker fundingWallet entries (2,152 such wallets). Every archive date from 2026-03-01 to 2026-08-07 was inflated by ~1,390-1,452 wallets and is corrected; the six entries before it (2026-01-18 through 2026-02-16) predate the regime, were never inflated, and are correctly left alone. SIDE EFFECT worth knowing before someone re-investigates it: the 2026-02-16 -> 2026-03-01 step widened from -528 to -2,007 as a result. That is not a new defect — the phantom inflation on the 03-01 side was partly masking a discontinuity that was already there, and both sides are now individually correct. The step lands on the 2026-02-28 MIN_TEL_RAW boundary (see that event, backfillStatus not-possible) and additionally spans a 13-day sampling gap, so it is expected to remain visible and unexplained-looking; the pre-2026-03-01 archive is a different measurement regime in several respects (see tasks/todo.md).

events.summary: MIN_TEL_RAW scan threshold lowered from 101 to 1 raw unit (PR #74) — wallets holding 1-100 raw TEL were never scanned by pull-holders-rpc.js before this date
events.backfillNote: REVISED 2026-08-21 — the 'not-possible' verdict below was wrong, and the fix supersedes it rather than amending it, so both are kept for the record. Original reasoning (2026-08-19): pre-2026-02-28 tel-holders.json snapshots never scanned wallets under 101 raw units (~1.01 TEL), so recomputing against the current threshold could only reclassify already-recorded wallets, not discover balances the original RPC scan never queried — concluded this was a permanent, RPC-replay-only limitation. That reasoning assumed recovery required archived STATE (eth_call at a historical block), which public nodes gate behind a paid tier. It does not: a token balance is fully determined by the Transfer logs preceding it, and logs are ordinary historical data, not state. scripts/rebuild-history-from-logs.js replays every TEL Transfer log from each chain's genesis via alchemy_getAssetTransfers and applies today's MIN_TEL_RAW=1 threshold uniformly across the whole range — recovering exactly the sub-1.01-TEL wallets the pre-2026-02-28 scans never wrote to any blob, no archived state needed. Verified: the 2026-02-16 → 03-01 step collapsed from -2,007 (with 2026-08-19's phantom-staker backfill layered on top — see the 2026-08-07 event) to +14, in line with ordinary day-to-day churn. holders-history.json has been fully rebuilt via this replay, 2026-01-01 onward; commit c5f6cd3's live holders-lite.json delta suppression is unaffected and still applies to that separate comparison.

supersededVerdict.backfillNote: Produces a real +5.42% totalHeld / holder-count jump between the 2026-02-16 and 2026-03-01 holders-history.json entries (the nearest snapshots either side of the change — there was no snapshot taken on 2026-02-28 itself). Unlike the two exclusion-list events above, this CANNOT be backfilled by scripts/recompute-history-from-git.js or any other git-history replay: pre-2026-02-28 tel-holders.json snapshots simply never scanned or recorded wallets with a raw balance under 101 units (~1.01 TEL) — that data was never written to any historical git blob, so there is nothing to recover it from. Recomputing against the current (lower) threshold can only change which already-recorded wallets count as retail vs. excluded; it cannot retroactively discover chain balances the original RPC scan never queried for. This is the one archive-wide discontinuity that is a genuine, permanent data-coverage boundary rather than a fixable classification bug — commit c5f6cd3 (2026-03-01, 'fix(pipeline): suppress deltas when MIN_TEL_RAW methodology changes') already suppresses the misleading +/- delta badge on the live holders-lite.json comparison for this reason; this entry documents the same boundary for the holders-history.json line chart, which has no equivalent suppression and will show a single unavoidable step at this date.

events.summary: Five previously-unlabelled addresses holding exactly 1,750,000,000 TEL relabelled from retail to category:escrow with confidence:medium ('assumed'). All are Telcoin Holdings-funded, have never sent a transaction, and were funded inside the same 2025-10-02..12-02 window as the confirmed Anchorage/BitGo escrow.
events.evidence: Origin: 100% traced to Telcoin Holdings ops / cold / bridge-hub Safes, no other funder. Behaviour: zero outflows ever; zero normal transactions (never even funded with ETH for gas), the same profile as Anchorage. Signature: each preceded by a 1,000 TEL test transfer then the bulk, as Anchorage (1,000 on 2025-09-24, then 2.5B on 10-01) and BitGo. Timing: funded 2025-10-24..12-01, interleaved with confirmed escrow legs, and 0x043a1639 shares 2025-11-27 with two BitGo Holdings legs. Arithmetic: 1,750,000,000 exactly, and combined with BitGo's Holdings-sourced 1,334,240,801 gives 3,084,240,801 — within 2.8% of the reported 3B Holdings escrow commitment.
events.limitation: Custodian identity is NOT established. These addresses have never sent a transaction, so nothing on-chain reveals who holds the keys; Blockscout returns no public tag. Note the same is true of Anchorage, whose name is owner-supplied and which carries no public tag either. confidence:medium records this and must not be promoted without a Telcoin disclosure naming the custodian.
events.circulatingImpact: None by design. No nonCirculatingOverride is set, because Holdings-sourced escrow stays circulating under existing policy (BitGo's Holdings portion is treated the same way). Only the retail/escrow bucket split moves.
events.backfillNote: Backfilled 2026-08-29 via scripts/backfill-escrow-vault-reclassification.js. All five vaults are fully funded and static (funded 2025-10-21..12-01, zero outflows since), so their combined 1,750,000,000 TEL balance is a KNOWN CONSTANT on every archived date -- a targeted delta, not a replay, and exact rather than approximate. Corrected in holders-history.json (233 of 235 entries, dates < 2026-08-28): combined + chains.ethereum totalBalance/retailHolderCount/holderCount/holderCountWithStakers/totalHeld; the 250M-500M distribution tier (both levels); combined concentration N in {50,100,250,500,1000} and ethereum concentration N in {25,50,100,250,500,1000}; cumulativeHolders. Also corrected: holders-ever-checkpoint.json (5 addresses removed from the ever-held set) and treasury-history.json (escrow category, 233 entries). ONE KNOWN, DELIBERATE GAP: combined concentration N=10 and N=25 could NOT be corrected exactly -- concentration is a strict top-N ranking, not a tier aggregate, and the combined 500M+/250M-500M population exceeds 25 on 101 of the 233 dates (peaks at 28, in 2026-05), so a flat subtraction there could silently be wrong by up to 1.75B on those specific dates. Left uncorrected rather than guessed; would need a full per-date wallet ranking (not stored in the archive) to close.
events.uiNote: Metric names must match the exact strings passed to getEventsAffecting: 'retail.count' (HolderGrowthWidget, DistributionAnalysisWidget, useHeadlineTiles), 'retail.balance' (DistributionAnalysisWidget, useHeadlineTiles) and 'totalHeld' (HolderGrowthWidget's balance chart). 'totalBalance'/'holderCount'/'escrow' are kept as documentation but are matched by no call site — adding a metric here that nothing queries silently produces no marker.
events.dateNote: The config edit was made 2026-08-29, but `date` must be the first DATA POINT that carries the new classification — the 2026-08-28 holders-history entry. getEventsAffecting requires eventMs <= toMs, and every chart's range ends at the archive's last entry, so an event dated after that entry sits outside every range and silently renders no marker at all.

events.summary: TEL v3 upgrade contracts TokenMigration (0x2703…2703) and MigrationVault (0x2222…3333) labelled category:escrow, and the pipeline now tracks legacy (2-decimal) + TEL v3 (18-decimal) balances per wallet. TokenMigration was an unlabelled retail wallet holding ~19.3B legacy TEL (the largest 'holder' in the snapshot); the legacy TEL it holds in exchange for minted v3 is now netted out of it, so swapped TEL is counted once, as v3 in the swapper's wallet.
events.evidence: On-chain at 2026-10-19 03:44 UTC = 2026-10-18 23:44 ET (public RPC, all chains pinned to that instant): TokenMigration holds legacy TEL 3,779,440,827.66 (Ethereum) + 19,110,053,421.21 (Polygon) + 123,053,750.56 (Base) = 23,012,547,999.43; TEL v3 totalSupply is 3,557,333,552.74 + 19,271,543,982.98 + 183,445,719.33 = 23,012,323,255.05. The 224,744.38 difference is one Polygon transfer of legacy TEL into TokenMigration with no v3 mint (stranded, not swapped); every other legacy transfer into the contract shares its transaction with a v3 mint of the same amount. v3 crosses chains by burn-and-mint, so v3 supply nets to the swapped amount. Derivation and the full table: docs/TEL-CONTRACTS.md 'Supply accounting'.
events.limitation: Pre-2026-10-18 history is legacy-only, so for dates after the v3 deployment (2026-08-06) swapped TEL appears as a growing balance on TokenMigration with no v3 counterpart, and the swappers' own balances fall by the same amount. Re-labelling TokenMigration backwards without ALSO adding the v3 holdings would remove up to ~19B of swapped TEL from retail on those dates, which is a worse error than leaving it, so those rows are left as published. v3 holdings by date are recoverable from v3 Transfer logs, but rebuilding every archived row from them needs the multi-GB per-chain transfer caches (data/rebuild-transfers-*.ndjson, gitignored) that are not available to CI or to this change. Rows before the v3 deployment are unaffected (v3 = 0, TokenMigration did not exist).
events.circulatingImpact: Retail/escrow split and holder counts move on the first pipeline run that tracks v3; total supply stays 100B. Escrow gains only the stranded remainder on TokenMigration (~224,744 TEL), because the swapped legacy is netted out, not bucketed. No nonCirculatingOverride is set.

breaksSeries.note: Methodology change (TEL v3 and staking now tracked) — not a market move

events.backfillNote: NOT BACKFILLED, deliberately: the committed archive has no v3 balances, so applying the new classification backwards (scripts/recompute-history-from-git.js) would delete swapped TEL from retail without adding it back as v3 and fabricate a step on the first v3-aware row. The first v3-aware row is the next pipeline run after this change; expect one step there, where TEL moves from the TokenMigration wallet to the individual wallets that hold the v3 (retail.balance roughly flat, holderCount up, cexBalance/DEX unchanged). Closing this gap exactly means replaying v3 + legacy transfer logs per archived date (data/date-blocks.json maps dates to blocks) against the full transfer caches.

events.summary: The Polygon holder scan started at block 21,500,000 although legacy TEL (Polygon) was deployed at block 11,264,036 and had already minted 6.49B and burned 3.69B TEL by block 21.5M. Balances are replayed from zero, so every early holder that has not moved since block 21.5M was missing: 298.4M TEL of Polygon supply (38.59B counted vs 38.89B on-chain). The scan now starts at the deployment block; old checkpoints are discarded and rebuilt.
events.evidence: eth_getLogs on Polygon TEL 0xdf7837de… over 11,264,036-21,499,999 (first Transfer at block 11,356,608): 6,493,106,321.70 TEL minted, 3,692,587,637.43 burned, 5,177 addresses with a positive balance at block 21.5M totalling ~2.84B at that block. Pipeline Polygon total before the fix: 38,591,385,281.67 TEL; Polygon totalSupply() at block 95,784,150: 38,889,754,532.20. Replaying 11.26M-21.5M and taking balanceOf() at block 95,784,150 for those 5,177 addresses (every other address keeps its scanned balance) gives 38,889,742,196.68, within 12,335.52 TEL (sub-dust-floor balances) of totalSupply().
events.limitation: Ethereum (from 4.6M) and Base (from block 100,000; first TEL transfer 25,614,028) were complete and are unchanged. Published history before this fix undercounts Polygon by roughly 0.3B TEL (~0.3% of supply) and the number of Polygon wallets by the early holders that had not moved since block 21.5M.
events.circulatingImpact: Polygon retail and combined retail balances increase by the early holders' balances; no address changed category. Total supply (Ethereum totalSupply) is unchanged.
events.backfillNote: Rebuilding history needs a full Polygon replay from block 11,264,036 at every archived date, which the transfer caches (which start at 21.5M) and keyless RPCs cannot supply; the pipeline's next full run only publishes the corrected current snapshot. History rows before that run keep the old Polygon figures.
events.uiNote: Polygon balances and the all-chains wallet count step up on the first refresh after this fix. That step is a data correction, not buying or new holders.
events.dateNote: Dated the day the correction shipped; the undercount was present for the whole published history.

events.summary: The TEL v3 StakingModule on Polygon (0x573105be…5731, EIP-1967 proxy of StakingModule 0xd12ba966…03ae) custodies stakers' TEL v3 — about 2.99B TEL on 2026-10-23. It was published as a single retail wallet in the 500M+ tier. Its receipt-token positions are now attributed to the 829 individual stakers (as is already done for the legacy staking contract) and the module itself is labelled staking-contract.
events.evidence: Sourcify verified source for the implementation 0xd12ba966cc3ebc87f1b8bcbf1fa3bfed397203ae: src/StakingModule.sol (stake/stakeFor/requestWithdrawal, ERC-20 receipt balances). At Polygon block 96,042,367: StakingModule totalSupply() 2,991,605,169.62, TEL v3 balanceOf(module) 2,991,605,169.62, totalPendingWithdrawal() 0. Replaying the module's own Transfer logs from its deployment block 93,048,895 gives 829 positive positions summing exactly to totalSupply().
events.limitation: Stakers' positions are counted at their staked amount; rewards or pending withdrawals that are not represented by receipts stay on the module (non-retail). Staked TEL now combines the legacy staking contract and the v3 StakingModule, deduped by staker.
